U.S. GAS exports and more generation erode surplus stocks

U.S. gas inventories have reverted to near normal for the time of year, eliminating the previous surplus, after exports accelerated and sustained low prices in the second and third quarters encouraged an increase in gas-fired generation. 

Working gas stocks in underground storage totalled 3,415 billion cubic feet on September 25 compared with 3,544 bcf on the same date a year earlier, according to data published by the U.S. Energy Information Administration. 

Inventories were still 54 bcf (+2% or +0.20 standard deviations) above the ten-year seasonal average but the surplus had narrowed sharply from its peak of 200 bcf (+7% or +0.57σ) at the start of July ...

The International Energy Agency is due to have talks Wednesday on plans for an emergency release of as much as 100 million barrels of diesel and crude inventories pledged by G7 leaders last week, according to people familiar with the matter.

The IEA’s Governing Board will have an initial discussion about the releases to establish more clarity on how to take the process forward, the people said. It’s not clear whether any decisions will be taken at this meeting. The board will convene next week for its regularly scheduled quarterly gathering, the people said.

A tropical system developing in the Bay of Campeche may reach the US Gulf Coast this weekend, threatening heavy rain while potentially skirting major oil and gas hubs.

The swirl of showers and winds has a 90% chance of becoming a tropical depression in the coming days, the US National Hurricane Center said on Monday. A depression is the weakest of a class of storms that also includes tropical storms and hurricanes. It won’t be named until its winds reach 39 miles (63 kilometers) per hour and would likely be called Isaias.

#Commodities
Softs: #Sugar futures jumped 4% on Monday to a 2024 high of 20.7 cents per pound, extending their recent strong run. While the latest move was underpinned by a 5% rally in the Brazilian real, an intensifying El Niño is adding to supply concerns, with excessive rainfall threatening production in Brazil while drought risks are rising in India and Thailand. These developments could potentially turn an expected sugar surplus into a deficit already this season. #Cocoa futures rose 3.5% on Monday, extending their weekly gain to 8%, as heavy rains in West Africa slowed sales, with flooded roads disrupting transport and wet conditions affecting bean quality.
Oil: #Brent traded lower on Monday, before bouncing ahead of USD 100 in Asia, as Gulf producers moved larger volumes through the Strait of Hormuz, with additional supply flowing through Saudi Arabia’s reopened East-West pipeline. Yet prices remain above USD 100 as a sizeable geopolitical risk premium persists amid the continued threat of renewed flare-ups. Iran, meanwhile, remains effectively blocked in, with dozens of laden tankers stranded along its coastline.
#Gold trades near key support just above USD 4,100, with macroeconomic headwinds from rising real yields and dollar strength continuing to weigh on investor appetite and fuel further long liquidation from hedge funds. With limited US economic data due this week, market focus will likely remain on the dollar, yields and ongoing political and fiscal turmoil in the Eurozone. A break below support just above USD 4,100 could signal a deeper retracement, while initial resistance is seen around USD 4,230.
